title: docs(site): give a doc page a short sidebar label (navTitle) distinct from its title
body:
Fixes #12311

A doc page's frontmatter `title` was the only string the site had. This adds `navTitle` — the page tree's own short label — and pins the separation so the long, search-intent title stays on every surface that is not the sidebar. This card is the **mechanism only**: no page title is rewritten here, which is #12237's 176-row table sitting `Blocked-by:` this one.

## The measurement this was built on

Re-measured in this worktree on `origin/main` @ `3b2a3f640`, not carried over from the card.

**Frontmatter corpus** — `content/docs/**/*.mdx`: **405 pages**; the only keys in use anywhere are `title` (405) and `description` (405); 0 pages carry any nav-label field. Independently reproduced by `check-doc-frontmatter`, which now prints it: *"405 page(s) parse with yaml@2.9.0 — 190 hand-written + 215 generated under references/"*.

**Consumers of `page.data.title`** — the card said four, the card's own repair comment said six, and the code says **eleven read sites across six surfaces**, plus the page tree:

| surface | sites |
|---|---|
| SERP `title` / OG / twitter metadata | `page.tsx:211`, `:216`, `:227` (OG image alt), `:233` |
| on-page `h1` (`DocsTitle`) | `page.tsx:150` |
| JSON-LD `TechArticle` headline/name | `page.tsx:123`, `:124` |
| JSON-LD `BreadcrumbList` leaf | `page.tsx:95` — **and, until this PR, the page tree** |
| `llms.txt` / `llms-full.txt` / `.mdx` | `app/llms.txt/route.ts:10`, `lib/source.ts:55` (`getLLMText`) |
| Open Graph card image | `app/og/docs/[...slug]/route.tsx:18` |
| sidebar / page tree | `lib/source.ts` — `loader()` |

Two disagreements with the card's list are recorded rather than smoothed over. `generateMetadata` is four reads, not one. And `lib/source.ts:55` `getLLMText` is a **seventh** consumer the card's table did not name — it is what `llms-full.txt` and the `/llms.mdx/docs/...` endpoints emit, so the card's "llms.txt" row covers one of the three agent-facing endpoints.

## Does `fumadocs-core@16.14.4` already ship this?

**No key. Yes hook.** Read out of the installed package:

- `dist/source/schema.js` — `pageSchema` is `{ title, description, icon, full, _openapi }`; `metaSchema` is `{ title, pages, pagesIndex, description, root, defaultOpen, collapsible, icon }`. No nav label on either.
- `dist/loader-*.js`, `buildFile()` — the page-tree builder destructures exactly `{ title, description, icon }` off a page. Nothing else on a page can become a tree label.
- `meta.json` `pages` entries parse into five forms only: a path, `...` / `z...a` rest, a `---Separator---`, a `!exclude` or `...extract` prefix, and a `[Name](url)` link. The link form builds a node with **no** `$ref` and a hand-written URL, bypassing page resolution and the loader's i18n URL generation — a raw link, not a per-page label override.
- Grep for `sidebarTitle`/`navTitle`/`navLabel`/`sidebar_label` across `dist/`: **zero hits**.

So the key had to be ours. What is **not** ours is the wiring: `PageTreeTransformer` is fumadocs' own extension point, and `transformPageTree: { file }` is exactly the shape its built-in icon plugin uses (`iconPlugin`, `dist/icon-*.js`). This is an extension through the library's published seam, not a transform bolted around it.

That answer is now a live assertion rather than a note: `check-docs-nav-label` re-reads both stock schemas on every run and **reds when fumadocs ships a first-class equivalent**, saying migrate — so ours cannot quietly become the thing nobody migrated.

## What landed

**`apps/docs/source.config.ts`** — `docsSchema = pageSchema.extend({ navTitle: z.string().optional() })`, mirroring the `blogSchema` extension two declarations below.

**`apps/docs/lib/nav-title.ts`** (new) — the single resolution point and the mechanism's documentation. `navLabel()` returns the declared label when it is a non-blank string and `title` otherwise; `navTitlePlugin()` applies it to page-tree nodes. **The `title` fallback is stated there and at no read site** — no `??` at a consumer, which is the shape AGENTS.md Prime Directive `12` rejects. Blank, `null` (what YAML gives a valueless `navTitle:`) and non-strings all fall back, because an invisible sidebar entry is worse than a long one.

**`apps/docs/lib/source.ts`** — one line: the plugin joins `lucideIconsPlugin()` in the docs `loader()`.

**`apps/docs/app/[lang]/docs/[[...slug]]/page.tsx`** — `getBreadcrumbItems(..., { includePage: false })`. This is the one place the card's own acceptance criterion could have been silently violated, and it is worth reading closely.

## The leak the card did not name: the JSON-LD breadcrumb reads the tree

`docsTrail()` builds `BreadcrumbList` from `source.pageTree`, not from `page.data.title` — its docblock said so deliberately: *"a crumb and its sidebar entry are the same node with the same label."* With `includePage: true`, the **leaf** crumb was the page's tree node. Give that node a short `navTitle` and the short label lands in structured data a crawler reads — on the exact surface #12243 exists to improve, with nothing failing.

`includePage: false` moves the leaf onto the function's existing tail push, `{ name: page.data.title, url: canonical }`. **Behaviour-identical on today's corpus**, and identical for a structural reason rather than by inspection — traced through `getBreadcrumbItemsFromPath`:

- *non-index page in folder F*: before, `[F, page-node]`; after, `[F]` + the tail push. The page node's `name` **is** `page.data.title`, so the same pair either way.
- *index page of folder F*: fumadocs skips the folder crumb when `item.index === path[i+1]`, so before it was `[page-node]` and after it is `[]` + the tail push. Same pair again.

Ancestors are unaffected in both cases: they are folders, labelled from their own `meta.json` `title`, and all 35 `meta.json` files under `content/docs` declare one.

## Pinning the separation

The whole value of the split is a string staying out of places nobody re-reads, and every way of losing it is silent — a consumer reading the key "because it is nicer", a second fallback appearing at a read site, a resolver that stops falling back (which costs **all 405** pages their sidebar label), a plugin dropped from `loader()` leaving the key declared and inert. None of those breaks a type, a link, a build or a test.

`scripts/check-docs-nav-label.mjs` (new, wired into `lint.yml`) states the invariant conditionally and carries six legs:

- **A** — `navTitle` appears in **code** in exactly the two files that declare and resolve it. Comments are masked through `js-comment-mask.mjs`, so the mechanism's own prose can name the key freely while a read cannot hide in a comment.
- **B** — the resolver is **executed**, not read: seven fallback cases plus four page-tree node cases, through Node's TypeScript type stripping.
- **C** — the plugin is actually wired into `loader()`.
- **D** — the breadcrumb leaf does not come from the page tree.
- **E** — all four `title`-consuming files still read `page.data.title`.
- **F** — fumadocs still ships no nav-label key.

`--self-test` (25 assertions) observes every leg red as well as green. Leg B's mutants are **real modules written to a temp dir and imported the same way the real one is**: a resolver that stopped falling back, an inert plugin, one that clobbers a titleless page's path-derived name, and one exporting nothing. Legs A/C/D/E run over synthetic file maps — including two negative controls that matter, the key named in **prose** (silent, as intended) and the identifier `navTitlePlugin` (silent — the word boundary is load-bearing).

`scripts/check-doc-frontmatter.mjs` gains the docs root's key contract. That gate asserts set equality between `source.config.ts`'s extensions and its own contracts, so extending the docs schema **required** it: its self-test previously asserted *"the docs root is still handed `pageSchema` unextended"*. Both roots are now `pageSchema.extend(...)` and the parity leg runs over both, so an extension key added in `source.config.ts` and nowhere else reds on either root instead of arriving unowned.

## Verification

All commands run in the worktree; the union below was run on the final commit **`a5eb6cc8d`**.

| what | result |
|---|---|
| `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs` — full derived family, **41 commands** | 39 exit 0; 2 exit **3** = NOT MEASURED, not red (see below) |
| the 8 changeset-triggered families, re-derived after writing the changeset | 8/8 exit 0 |
| `node scripts/check-docs-nav-label.mjs --self-test` | `25 assertions` |
| `node scripts/check-doc-frontmatter.mjs --self-test` | `85 assertions` |
| `node scripts/check-doc-frontmatter.mjs` | `405 page(s)` parse; `navTitle` a string on the 0 that declare one |
| `pnpm --filter @objectstack/docs typecheck` (`fumadocs-mdx && next typegen && tsc --noEmit`) | exit 0 |
| `pnpm lint` — repo-wide `eslint . --no-inline-config`, **not narrowed** | exit 0 |
| `pnpm check:nul-bytes`, `check:docs-single-h1`, `check:doc-anchors`, `check:doc-authoring` | 4/4 exit 0 |

The two exit-3 results are the repo's PREREQUISITE-NOT-MET code, and both say in their own verdict text that they are not findings: `check-test-completeness` needs a test-run log the family invocation cannot give it, and `check:type-check-debt --re-measure` refuses without a built workspace closure. Neither is reachable from this diff — nothing here touches a ledgered package.

Two things checked rather than assumed, because "typecheck passed" is a claim about a program and not about a file:

- `tsc --noEmit --listFiles` names `source.config.ts`, `lib/nav-title.ts`, `lib/source.ts` and `app/[lang]/docs/[[...slug]]/page.tsx` — the new file really is in the program.
- the generated `.source/source.config.mjs` carries `navTitle: z.string().optional()`, so the extension reached the docs build's own compiled config rather than only the TypeScript.

**No page changed.** No `content/docs/**` fixture was needed: leg B drives the resolver over a synthetic storage, and `check-doc-frontmatter` independently reports 0 of 405 pages declaring the key — so "all 405 keep working" is two measurements rather than an argument.

## Where #12237 cites this from

`apps/docs/lib/nav-title.ts`'s header, which carries the contract, a worked frontmatter example and the surface table. That was chosen over a new page under `content/docs/**`: that tree is the product documentation, and a contributor-facing authoring rule added there becomes a 406th page needing its own `meta.json` entry and its own title. The header sits at the resolution point, so it cannot drift from the code, and the frontmatter key is additionally typed in `check-doc-frontmatter`'s docs key contract — the gate that speaks to a frontmatter author when they get it wrong.

## Not addressed here

`#12237` remains open and is not touched by this PR — the 176 title rewrites are its own card, and its PR carries the rule plus the before/after table.
